cards.explanation: The answer is covenant. God says, “I will establish My covenant between Me and you…” A covenant is a binding promise, and this one comes straight from God Almighty. He adds, “…and I will multiply you exceedingly.” That is a LOT of multiplying, friends, so I bet Abram needed a minute, and he gets one. He falls facedown right there (Genesis 17:3).

The answer is many nations. God says, “You will be the father of many nations.” Not one nation. Not two. MANY, friends. Abram is ninety-nine, and God is talking about a family tree with a whole lot of branches.

The answer is Abraham. God says, “No longer will you be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations.” The new name comes with a reason attached. God doesn't just hand over a new name, friends, He tells Abraham why.

The answer is kings. God says, “I will make nations of you, and kings will descend from you.” Nations and kings in the same breath. Abraham is facedown on the ground, and God is still adding to the list.

The answer is True. God says, “I will establish My covenant as an everlasting covenant between Me and you and your descendants after you…” Everlasting means it isn't a one-batch deal, friends. It reaches Abraham's family down the line, and God says He will be their God too.

The answer is Canaan. God says, “…I will give the land where you are residing…” and then names it: “…all the land of Canaan…” Abraham is living there right now as a resident. God is saying it will belong to his family for good, friends.

The answer is to be circumcised. God says, “Every male among you must be circumcised.” That's the part Abraham and his family keep, friends. God makes the covenant promise, and this is how they show they belong to it.

The answer is True. God says, “You are to circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and this will be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.” A sign is something you can see. This one marks every male in the covenant family, friends.

The answer is False. God says every male must be circumcised, “…including those born in your household and those purchased from a foreigner…” Then He repeats it in verse 13. Born in the household or bought, friends, the covenant sign covers them.

The answer is that he will be cut off from his people. God says, “…he will be cut off from his people; he has broken My covenant.” The text puts those two things together right there. God treats this as a serious matter, friends, so we keep it serious too.

The answer is a son. God says, “…I will bless her and will surely give you a son by her.” Sarah is Abraham's wife, and the promise runs through her. Notice the word “surely,” friends. God isn't hedging.

The answer is True. God says Sarah “…will be the mother of nations; kings of peoples will descend from her.” Sarah gets a new name and a promise to match, friends. She's not a bystander in this covenant.

The answer is whether a man of a hundred can have a child. Abraham says to himself, “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old?” He laughs while he's down on the ground. I think he's trying to wrap his head around it, friends, and honestly, so would I.

The answer is that Ishmael might live under God's blessing. Abraham says, “O that Ishmael might live under Your blessing!” Ishmael is Abraham's son, and Abraham wants good for him. I think that's a dad talking, friends.
The answer is Isaac. God says, “Your wife Sarah will indeed bear you a son, and you are to name him Isaac.” Naming a baby usually takes a whole lot of debating, friends. Here God just says the name.

The answer is twelve. God says Ishmael “…will become the father of twelve rulers, and I will make him into a great nation.” God answers Abraham's request with a promise to bless Ishmael, in His own words. That's a lot of family to feed, friends.

The answer is False. God says, “…I will establish My covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time next year.” He also says He has heard Abraham about Ishmael and will surely bless him (verse 20). Ishmael is blessed, friends, and the covenant goes to Isaac.

The answer is at this time next year. God says Sarah will bear Isaac “…at this time next year.” Not someday, friends. NEXT YEAR. That's a date you can put on the calendar. Right before this, Abraham laughs and asks, “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old?” (Genesis 17:17), and God answers with a timeline, a short one.

The answer is that very day. The text says, “On that very day Abraham took his son Ishmael and all those born in his household or purchased with his money…” There's no sleeping on it and no putting it off, friends. I've seen people take longer to answer a text message.

The answer is male. Abraham circumcises Ishmael and “…every male among the members of Abraham’s household…” just as God had told him. He does what God said, to everyone God said. That's a full day of work, friends.
